verdict.rationale: Netlify's own copy says you can drop a project folder to deploy, with drag-and-drop listed as a start option alongside Git, so no repo is required. It also says new projects stay private until you choose to publish, which covers the privacy part of the story. missing for 10: in-depth first-party docs on the private-until-publish mechanism (the evidence is short marketing copy that describes privacy per project, not per deployment), and independent or hands-on corroboration of the folder-upload private-deploy flow.

support.subject: As a developer, I can deploy a project by uploading a folder of files directly, with no Git repo required and the new deployment kept private until I choose to publish it

citations.quote: Drop your project folder and deploy in seconds. New projects stay private until you choose to publish.
Start a new project with an AI agent, a Git repository, or drag and drop.
Deploy to a global CDN in seconds, then choose when to make your project public.
Deploy directly from your working directory.
